title: A task shows the sessions that ran it, on one clock
description:
## As asked

Repository: JKershaw/LinearViewer (Harbour).

**What this is for.** The loop Harbour runs is made of sessions: which ones run, what kind each is, which model runs it, how long it takes and what it costs. Seen together for one task, they show where the time and money went and where the work waited. John was looking at a drawing of one real task's sessions (LIN-4393, removing the size-of-the-move setting). It showed its eight sessions on one clock, each with its cost and duration, with the held orchestrator's wakes, the resumed part of the build and the merge time marked. He said: "'One real task, session by session' is fantastic as a visual! I'd love to see future versions of this, which actually optimise the graph of nodes, to get the results we're aiming for." In this project, the results we're aiming for are tasks that leave the codebase cleaner, with no new mess, at a falling cost, asking the person only what is theirs to decide. Today that picture is put together by hand, for one task. This asks Harbour to show it for every task, so the graph of sessions can be seen, and in time optimised, toward those results.

**What we want.** For any task, a person can see the sessions that ran it as one picture on one clock: which ran, in what order and alongside which others, what kind each was (for example a fresh worker, a held orchestrator and when it was woken, a session resumed), which model ran it, how long it took, what it cost, and when the work merged. Harbour already records each session's kind, model, timing and cost.

**Context.** LIN-4341 (Settings › Costs) shows where a workspace's money goes over a period; this is one task's view of its own sessions.

**Questions:** settle engineering questions yourself, and record why. Raise a ruling only for John's calls: how big a move is, what's spent, removing a step, the order of work, and authority.

**Done when** a person can open any task and see, in one picture on one clock, every session that ran it with its kind, model, time and cost, and when it merged (if it has); and it reads well on desktop and phone.

*End of what was asked. Steps write below this line; nothing above it changes.*

## Size of the move

**Size:** consolidate the decision this task touches
**Why:** Delivers the one-clock session picture for every task, first settling that a task's own views read its whole life rather than the 30-day reporting window, since otherwise tasks older than a month show no sessions.
**Cuts:**

* Guests on a shared link see the picture without spend, as John ruled: "every session that ran it with its kind, model, time and cost"

**Decided by:** a ruling

## Design (chosen approach)

The picture is server-rendered lanes built from the one cost read. It is a new **"Sessions on one clock"** section under Stages; Stages stays. The full analysis is in the design comment (10 Nov).

* **One per-task read, whole life.** Lift the `/cost` route's inline fetch (own rows, founder identity, lineage siblings, `readCost({ perDispatch: true })`) into one lib reader that the route and the task page both call. Name the rule in `lib/read-horizon.js`: a task's own reads cover its whole life; published reporting windows stay at 30 days (the size ruling). `/cost/:identifier` adopts it, and says so in `window`.
* **Working spans from the one split.** `dispatchesOf` gains `firstRequestAt` and `lastRequestAt` per dispatch, the min and max `at` of the records split rule C already assigns to it, or null when it has none. These are additive on `/cost`. Nothing else reassigns usage, and the census gets no new exemptions.
* **One role helper.** A new module returns `wake`, `resumed`, `orchestration` or `work` from `kind`, `followUpTo` and `ORCHESTRATION_KINDS`. Held means an orchestration base with wakes; fresh means a work base. Stages' `groupSessions` switches to it with unchanged output. It is tested against `DISPATCH_KINDS` and `ROW_ONLY_KINDS` (lesson in runs-and-dispatch.md, LIN-4376).
* **Pure view model.** It turns lineages, the merge time and now into lanes, segments, marks, a scale and totals:
  * solid working segments per dispatch;
  * a thin held line;
  * a running open end;
  * wake and resume ticks;
  * a merge rule;
  * "working times unknown" outlines for lineages without records, never a guessed bar.

  Gaps with no work longer than a threshold fold into labelled breaks, and held lines still cross them. Totals follow the figure rule.
* **Renderer.** Positioned HTML lanes, not SVG and with no client layout maths. On desktop a label column (kind · model · took / worked · cost) sits beside the track. On a phone (< 600 px, CSS only) the label sits above a full-width track on the same clock. Each lane is a `<details>` listing its dispatches, with an accessible `<summary>` name (front-end-pages lesson). Dollars go through `formatUsd`.
* **Spend gating.** One `withoutSpend` strip, applied by the routes for `viewer === 'guest'` (`/t/:token` and its fragment), before rendering. Owners and members see spend (John's ruling).
* **Merge time.** It comes from the close-out events read the loader already makes (`prMergedAt`), falling back to the PR status's `merged_at`. If neither is known, the page says "merged, time not recorded".
* **Freshness.** The page load renders the section. A fragment endpoint repaints it when the poll's track changes, or every 60 s while a session runs. The pinned `/state` key set is unchanged.
* **Founded-elsewhere lineages.** Lineages with a member on this task but a founder elsewhere are drawn and marked "counted under LIN-X". Their cost is shown but not added to this task's total, and attribution does not change.
* **Not reused:** `timeline-zoom.js`**.** Its bounds are now-anchored with a 24-hour cap on a linear scale, and the ask needs no zoom.
* **Housekeeping.** The new lib files get homes in `docs/areas/areas.json`. Update `docs/architecture/source-map.md`, `public/llms.txt` (new `data-*`), the renderer golden and the `/cost` route tests.
* **Tests.** A LIN-4393 fixture: eight lanes, the autopilot held about 63 min with five wakes, the implementation with its `leftover` resume, the two surveys side by side, and the merge rule. Plus cases for times unknown, running, multi-day breaks, founded elsewhere, guest stripping, and the e2e at 390 px.

**Cuts:** none beyond John's guest ruling.

## Implementation Plan

*Plan pass, 10 Nov, at* `b315e0e8f` *(HEAD is origin/main). Re-grounded:* `git log --since=2026-11-08T20:03:53Z` *over every file the ticket, surveys and design name is empty. This plan builds on the Design comment (10 Nov) and both surveys. Where it departs from them, it says so and why (see "Departures").*

### What this is for, and what done looks like

Harbour's loop is made of sessions. Seeing one task's sessions on one clock shows where its time and money went and where it waited. Today John's LIN-4393 drawing is made by hand. Done is the ticket's own line: **"a person can open any task and see, in one picture on one clock, every session that ran it with its kind, model, time and cost, and when it merged (if it has); and it reads well on desktop and phone."**

To John, done looks like this. LIN-4393's task page has a "Sessions on one clock" section that matches his drawing: eight lanes, the autopilot held about 63 min with five wakes and about 6 min of work, the implementation with its `leftover` resume, the two surveys side by side, and a merge rule. Each lane shows its kind, model, time taken versus time worked, and cost. A task from more than 30 days ago shows its sessions too. The same picture reads at 390 px. A shared `/t/` link shows it without dollars.

### Cuts to `## As asked`

One, already ruled: "every session that ran it with its kind, model, time and cost" is not delivered in full to guests, because guests see no cost (John, 10 Nov: "Owner and members see spend; guests see the picture without dollars"). There are no other cuts.

These are not cuts. The picture names them rather than hiding them:

* A session from before request records existed is drawn with its known start and end, marked "working times unknown".
* A merge Harbour never timed says "merged, time not recorded".
* A lineage cut off by `LINEAGE_QUERY_LIMIT` says "not complete" instead of showing a partial sum.

DECISION: no new cut needs a ruling. No BLOCKED.

### Which way, and why

**Shape A from the design:** server-rendered lanes over the one cost read, as a new section under Stages. Set aside:

* **B, client layout:** two copies of the scale-with-breaks rule, and a guest page that is empty until the script runs.
* **C, Live Console with a task filter:** no per-dispatch cost and no working spans, a now-anchored 24 h window, and adding cost would be a second cost path.
* **D, one session-graph model for all three views:** retiring Stages or Live Console is removing a step, which needs a ruling.

This change routes around no cause. The two causes it meets are fixed where they live:

* A task's own views read a 30-day reporting window. Fixed in the read rule (`lib/read-horizon.js`).
* No dispatch has an end time. Fixed in the one split that already assigns request records to dispatches (`dispatchesOf`).

### Departures from the design (checked at HEAD)

1. **Stages'** `groupSessions` **does not switch to the role helper.** It asks one question, `ORCHESTRATION_KINDS.has(kind)` (`lib/task-page-loader.js` `groupSessions`). It already reads the one set, defined in `lib/run-view.js` and re-exported by `lib/effort-readout.js`.
   * The helper checks `resumed` before `orchestration`. So a ci-wake `custom` row with `followUpTo` would leave Stages' check-ins and become a Stage of its own. Stages' output would change, which the constraints forbid.
   * Switching to a kind-only predicate would add a layer and remove nothing.
   * The helper imports the same set, so there is still one fact.
   * Live Console's wake folding (`lib/live-console.js`) is left as it is. It is not this task's, and the leftover step records it in the runs-and-dispatch notes.
2. **The reader cannot split lineages by founder itself.** `groupLineageMembership` may only be imported by the files listed in `FOLD_IMPORTERS` (`tests/unit/cost-read-census.test.js`), and `workerSessions` rows do not carry their founder.
   * So `readCost` gains an opt-in, passed only by the task timeline. It returns a separate `foundedElsewhere` list beside the unchanged figures: lineages founded on another issue that have a fetched member tagged with this issue.
   * These are summarised by the same branches. Each carries `countedUnder` (the founder's identifier) and the itemIds tagged with this issue. They are never added to `pricedUsd` or `totalUsd`.
   * This adds no read. Today's fetch already loads these lineages, because this issue's identity rows name their anchors, and then `lineageRecordsOverRecords` drops them. `/cost` does not pass the flag.
3. **Design open question "which foreign rows carry this task's identifier" is answered.** `lib/dispatch-wake.js` stamps a wake row with the triggering child's `issueIdentifier` (`issueIdentifier: child.issueIdentifier || null`).
   * So when a parent's autopilot drives this task, the wakes this task's sessions caused are members of the parent's lineage and are tagged with this task. The foreign lane draws those tagged dispatches, and only they set the clock.
   * Checked live: `GET /dispatch?issueIdentifier=LIN-4393` lists its five wakes under LIN-4393. There the founder is the task itself.
4. **The PR-status fallback for the merge time needs a field that is not carried today.** The close-out's `pr` model (`deriveState` in `lib/run-evidence.js`) drops GitHub's `merged_at`. Add it as `pr.mergedAt`. This is additive.
5. **Open question on** `window` **is decided.** `/cost`'s `window` becomes `{ days: null, appCallsSince: null, scope: 'task-life' }`.
   * There is no day bound to report, and a number would be false. `scope` is the added key, placed last.
   * `lib/proxy-instructions.js` and `docs/proxy-integration.md` change with it.
6. **Whole life is an explicit bound, not a missing one.** `listInHorizon` turns a missing `since` into the 30-day start (`lib/llm-call-log.js`). So "pass no since" would quietly stay at 30 days.
   * The named rule in `lib/read-horizon.js` exports a task-life bound that admits every record. The reader passes it as `since` to both `listHistory` calls and to `listInHorizon`.
   * The index-backed range queries keep their shape, and a missing bound still means 30 days.
7. **"Running" comes from the page model.** `workerSessions` rows carry no status.
   * A lane is running when one of its dispatch itemIds is an open session in the model (`isOpenState`, `lib/task-state.js`).
   * A session's `loopId` is the dispatch item id (`lib/pipeline-loops.js`, `loopId: item.id`). The reader takes the open ids from its caller, and both the page load and the fragment have them.
8. **One merge rule, read by the timeline reader itself.**
   * Each merged PR in this issue's close-out events (`merged: true`, de-duplicated by `prUrl`) gets a merge mark at its `prMergedAt`.
   * If no event has a `prMergedAt` and the close-out says merged, use `pr.mergedAt`. That is on page load only: the poll and the fragment never fetch from GitHub.
   * Otherwise, if merged, show the words without a rule.
   * On a merged task's page load this repeats the indexed per-issue `listForIssue` read that `readMergedBy` makes. That is accepted so the page and the fragment share one rule. The builder may pass in the loader's events instead, as long as the rule function is the same.

### The shape, in landing order

`needs multiple sessions`: two parts, each landing and verified on its own, Part 1 first. One session would lose track of Part 1's published-API edges (the `/cost` window tests, the cost-replay goldens, the instructions text) while building Part 2's page, routes and browser poll.

**Part 1: the per-task read.** No UI. Its own PR.

* `lib/read-horizon.js`: the named rule, with the header rewritten. Published reporting windows (periodicals, `/kpis`, workspace spend, pipeline loops) stay at 30 days. A task's own reads (`/cost/:identifier`, the task page's timeline) cover its whole life. Drop `/cost` from the header's 30-day list.
* New file `lib/task-cost-read.js`. Move the fetch now inline in the `/cost` route (`routes/proxy-compute.js`, own rows → founder identity → siblings → `readCost({ perDispatch: true })`) there unchanged in substance, bounded by the task-life rule. Keep the truncation warning, and also return it as a flag so the picture can say "not complete". The route becomes a caller and keeps its validation, 400s and wire key order.
* `dispatchesOf` (`lib/cost-read.js`): each entry gains `firstRequestAt` and `lastRequestAt` (ISO). They are the min and max `at` of the records split rule C gives that entry, or null when it owns none with a time.
* `readCost` gains the `foundedElsewhere` opt-in (Departure 2).
* Correct the comment in `lineageRecordsOverRecords` that says "every fetched member comes from a since-bounded read". The task reads are no longer since-bounded. The guard still applies when `windowStart` is passed.
* `docs/areas/areas.json`: add `task-cost-read` to the runs-and-dispatch pattern. Update `docs/architecture/source-map.md`. Update `lib/proxy-instructions.js` and `docs/proxy-integration.md` for the window and the new fields.

**Part 2: the picture.** Its own PR, built on Part 1.

* New file `lib/session-roles.js`: `roleOf({ kind, followUpTo })` returns `wake`, `resumed`, `orchestration` or `work`, in that order, using the imported `ORCHESTRATION_KINDS`. A lineage reads as held when its base is orchestration and it has wakes, and as fresh when its base is work.
* New file `lib/task-timeline.js`. A pure `taskTimeline({ sessions, foundedElsewhere, merges, openItemIds, now })` returns `{ lanes, scale, marks, totals }`. It also holds `withoutSpend(timeline)` and `createTaskTimelineReader(deps)`, which composes `readTaskCost` (with no app-call summary), the close-out events and `taskTimeline`. What the plan fixes, beyond the design's list:
  * A lane runs from the lineage's `dispatchedAt` to `dispatchedAt + durationMs`. With no end, a running lane is open to now. A lane that has no end and is not running stops at its last known request or dispatch, and says "end not recorded".
  * Each dispatch's working segment is `[firstRequestAt, lastRequestAt]`, with a minimum visible width. A dispatch with no records gets a tick and no bar. A lineage with `dispatches: null` gets the "working times unknown" outline.
  * The total is the own read's `totalUsd`. When that is null, show "not complete" with the priced part named as priced, never shown as a bare total. Founded-elsewhere lanes show their own figure with "counted under LIN-X" and are left out of the total.
  * The break threshold starts at 10 min or 15 % of the span. The builder tunes it against the LIN-4393 fixture, which is its witness.
* New file `lib/render-task-timeline.js` (front-end-pages by its `render` prefix):
  * Positioned HTML, with no SVG and no layout maths in the browser. Below 600 px the label goes above a full-width track (CSS only).
  * Each lane is a `<details>`. Its `<summary>` carries a full accessible name. This follows the front-end-pages lesson "A control a page renders per row … needs its own accessible name" (`docs/areas/front-end-pages.md`, Design & Interface Review, 8 Nov).
  * Dollars go through `formatUsd` only. Add `data-testid`, `data-role`, `data-kind` and `data-state`. No cost appears in any attribute when the model has none.
* `lib/task-page-loader.js`: new injected dep `readTaskTimeline`.
  * `loadTaskPage` calls it and sets `model.timeline`. `loadTaskState` never calls it, so a quiet poll spends no cost read and the pinned `/state` keys do not change.
  * A failed read gives the section a short "sessions could not be read" line, and the page still renders.
* `lib/render-task-page.js`: the section goes under Stages. Stages' markup is unchanged.
* Routes:
  * `routes/task-page.js` adds `GET /workspace/:urlKey/api/task/:identifier/timeline`, which returns the fragment for owners and members.
  * `routes/task-share.js` applies `withoutSpend` before rendering on `/t/:token`, and adds `GET /t/:token/timeline`, which goes through the same `resolveScopedRecord`, applies `withoutSpend`, then `maskFragment`.
  * Each fragment takes the open ids from `loader.loadTaskState`, which reads stored facts only.
  * Wire the reader in `server.js`.
* `public/task-page.js`: fetch the fragment URL (a data attribute on the section) when the poll's `trackHtml` changes, or every 60 s while a lane is `data-state="running"`.
* `lib/run-evidence.js`: `pr.mergedAt` (Departure 4).
* `docs/areas/areas.json`: add `session-roles` and `task-timeline` to runs-and-dispatch. Update `docs/architecture/source-map.md`, and `public/llms.txt` for the new `data-*` attributes.

### Every place the behaviour lives

* **"A task's own read covers its whole life."** Repeat the search with `grep -rln "readHorizonStart\|inReadWindow\|READ_HORIZON" lib routes`. It finds 22 files.
  * In scope: `/cost/:identifier` and the new timeline read.
  * Out of scope, because they describe the run page's 30-day reach rather than reading a task: `inReadWindow` in `lib/task-page-loader.js`, `lib/home-row-states.js`, `routes/workspace-api-run-evidence.js`, and `lib/render-task-page.js` ("older than 30 days: no run page"). Changing them means making the run page read whole life, which was not asked.
  * The rest are published reporting windows (kpis, periodicals, ship-biscuit, the stores' own range reads) and stay.
* **"What role a dispatch plays."** The new helper, used by the timeline. Out of scope:
  * Stages' set check, for the reason in Departure 1.
  * Live Console's wake folding (not this task's).
  * `lib/pipeline-churn.js`'s own set (a waiting entry the size does not take on).
  * `lib/run-view.js`'s step model (constraint).
* **"Guests see no dollars."** Three guest responses: `/t/:token`, `/t/:token/timeline` and `/t/:token/state`. The last carries no timeline and must stay that way. Its witness is below.
* **"Dollars only through the one formatter."** The census catches any other.

### Witnesses (each fails before the change, passes after)

* A lineage dispatched 40 days ago appears in `/cost/:identifier` and in the timeline. The LIN-3161 suite in `tests/unit/proxy-issue-cost-route.test.js` is rewritten to the new rule.
  * **Guard test:** the reporting surfaces' existing 30-day suites (periodicals, `/kpis`, pipeline loops) stay green unchanged. One new assertion: `listInHorizon` with no `since` still bounds to 30 days.
* Under split rule C, `firstRequestAt` and `lastRequestAt` hold: a late-posted record's `at` counts toward the dispatch it moves to, and a dispatch with no records reads null.
  * With and without the `foundedElsewhere` flag, the own figures are byte-identical. A foreign lane's cost is not in `pricedUsd`.
  * Regenerate the cost-replay goldens (`scripts/cost-replay.mjs`). Their change list names only `window` and the two new fields. The census stays green with no new entry.
* `session-roles` gives every kind in `DISPATCH_KINDS` and `ROW_ONLY_KINDS` a role, with `leftover` read as resumed. This follows the runs-and-dispatch lesson (LIN-4376). Stages' existing tests and the renderer golden are unchanged apart from the new section.
* **A LIN-4393 fixture** taken from the real `/cost` output (checked live: autopilot $0.84 over 3,795 s with five wakes; implementation $6.95 with a `leftover` resume) plus request records. It must show eight lanes, five wake ticks, about 6 min worked on the autopilot, two segments on the implementation and a merge rule.
  * Cases: times unknown, running (open end), a two-day gap folded into one labelled break with a held line crossing it, a foreign-founded lane, merged with no recorded time, and a truncated lineage reading "not complete".
* **Guest test:** fetch all three guest responses for a priced task. Assert no `$` figure and no cost attribute in any of them. It fails if any path skips the strip.
* **e2e:** a task page at 390 px has no horizontal scroll, labels sit above the tracks, and a lane opens to its dispatches.

### Likeliest ways this breaks

1. **A guest path left unstripped,** especially the new fragment, or a data attribute carrying cost. Caught by the guest test over all three responses.
2. **Silent drift in** `/cost` **figures** from the extraction or the whole-life change. Caught by the replay goldens' change list and the byte-identical figures test. Agents reading `totalUsd` for an old task will now see whole-life figures, which is the point. The instructions text says so.
3. **Working time read as wall time:** a held lane drawn solid, or a missing-records lane given a guessed bar. Caught by the LIN-4393 fixture (about 6 of 63 min worked) and the times-unknown case.

Recent history on these files bears on the build. The cost read has been tightening for a month: one read (LIN-4177), loads its own records (LIN-4226), dispatch order (LIN-4276), per-dispatch split (LIN-4263). Add to it, never beside it. The loader grew from 661 to 1,544 lines in a month, so keep timeline logic out of it. LIN-4393 (#2377) is the fixture's source.

Area notes applied: runs-and-dispatch's "Row-only kinds … tested against both" (LIN-4376) and its `lib/pipeline-churn.js` waiting entry (context, not scope); front-end-pages' per-row accessible name lesson; README's "give it a home in the same change".

plan-review due: yes. It needs more than one session, changes a published API's read window and replaces the test that guarded it, and touches the guest route.

comments.body:
## Survey open-0: LIN-4395 @ b315e0e8f

**Short version: most of the data already exists. What's hard is drawing time honestly, not gathering sessions.**

**Already there.** `GET /api/proxy/cost/:identifier` (`routes/proxy-compute.js:662`, `readCost` with `perDispatch` in `lib/cost-read.js`, LIN-4263) returns one `workerSessions` row per lineage. Each row has its kind, model, duration and cost, plus `dispatches[]` with each dispatch's own kind, `dispatchedAt`, model and USD. For LIN-4393 it returns exactly the eight sessions in John's drawing: the autopilot with its `wake` dispatches, the implementation with its `leftover` resume, and the rest. Merge time is in `close-out-events-store` (`prMergedAt`, read at `:406`). So the first version is a pure view model built on that read plus the merge time, not a new store.

**Why it will still be difficult:**

1. **The data has start times, not end times.** A lineage has `dispatchedAt` → `completedAt` (`durationMs`). A single dispatch inside it (a wake, a resume) has only its `dispatchedAt`. The autopilot's 63 minutes on LIN-4393 are mostly held and idle. A bar from start to end would make it look like the most expensive session when it cost $0.84 against the build's $6.95. Working time has to look different from held time, and that needs an end for each dispatch. `request-usage` records carry `at`, so the first and last request of each dispatch give its working span. Use that, not feedback markers. Dispatches with no records (older lineages, or ones with no usage posted) need an honest "times unknown" state, not a guessed bar.
2. **One clock can cover very different lengths.** A two-minute survey sits beside an hour-long held orchestrator, and a task that waited days on a ruling stretches the clock to days. On a linear scale, a phone shows slivers. The view needs shortened gaps (a marked break on the axis) and probably a list of sessions on narrow screens instead of a squeezed chart. Settle this before writing any markup.
3. **"Any task" runs into the 30-day read window.** `/cost` limits itself to `since` = `READ_HORIZON_DAYS`, and the task page filters loops with `inReadWindow` (`lib/task-page-loader.js:340`). History is kept for the life of the project (LIN-3163), and `lib/read-horizon.js` says the 30 days applies to published reporting windows, not to retention. A per-task view can reasonably read the whole lifetime, but that is a decision to make and write down. Without it, older tasks render empty.
4. **The page in place drops orchestration.** `run-view.js:87/129` filters `autopilot`/`wake` out of the run page. The held orchestrator and its wakes are the centre of this picture, so don't build it by extending the run page's step model. "Fresh / held / resumed" isn't a stored field either. It has to be derived from `kind`, `waitForFollowUps`, `followUpTo` and `wake` rows, in one place.
5. **Attribution.** A lineage counts under its founder's issue (`lib/lineage-membership.js`). An orchestrator that drives several tasks appears on only one of them.
6. **Context check:** LIN-4341 (Settings › Costs) is not on main at this commit, so there's no shared cost component to reuse yet. Don't wait for it.

**What I'd do first:** write a pure `taskTimeline({ workerSessions, records, mergedAt })` → lanes/segments/marks. Test it against a fixture of LIN-4393's real `/cost` output, check it against the hand drawing, and settle items 1–3 in that test. Then render it on the task page.

The ticket isn't pointed at a symptom. It is the instrument the later optimisation needs. Item 1 does matter beyond the picture, though: without working-versus-held time, an optimiser would read waiting as cost.

## Survey global: LIN-4395 @ b315e0e8f

**Where it lands.** The task page (`lib/task-page-loader.js` → `lib/render-task-page.js`, polled by `public/task-page.js`) and the cost read (`lib/cost-read.js`, served by `/cost` in `routes/proxy-compute.js`). They are moving in opposite directions. The cost read has been consolidating for a month: one read (LIN-4177), one dispatch order (LIN-4276), per-dispatch splits (LIN-4263), and a census (`tests/unit/cost-read-census.test.js`) that fails any surface that folds usage or formats dollars itself. The task page is growing fast: the loader went from 661 to 1,544 lines between 2026-10-08 and 2026-11-07, and the renderer from 641 to 1,015.

**This would be the third session picture, not the first.** The codebase already draws a task's sessions twice:
- The task page's **Stages** section (`buildTaskStages`/`groupSessions`, loader :445–528) lists every dispatch over the task's whole life (`horizon: 'all'`). Wakes and autopilot are folded in as "check-ins", and a superseded session's "continued" end is derived from `followUpTo` (`followUpDispatches`).
- The **Live Console timeline** (`buildTimeline`/`packTimelineRows`, `lib/live-console.js:740–900`) is already a one-clock swimlane. It folds wakes into `wakeMarkers` on the held run they resume, draws resume edges from `followUpTo`, and packs rows by session group. It has its own zoom math (`lib/timeline-zoom.js`) and a 24h window.

Done the obvious way, a new `taskTimeline` module would re-derive "held / woken / resumed" a third time. ## Design: LIN-4395 @ b315e0e8f

**Short version.** Draw the picture on the server from the one cost read, as its own section on the task page. One lane per session. Working time is solid, held time is a thin line, wakes are ticks, the merge is a rule. Long empty stretches fold into marked breaks. On a phone each lane puts its words above its bar, and every lane still sits on the same clock. The task's own read covers the task's whole life, as the size ruling says. The `/cost/:identifier` read switches to the same rule, so the two views of a task cannot disagree.

### Re-grounding

- Every file the ticket and the surveys name is unchanged since the ticket was filed: `git log --since=2026-11-08T20:03:53Z` over `lib/cost-read.js`, `lib/task-page-loader.js`, `lib/render-task-page.js`, `public/task-page.js`, `routes/proxy-compute.js`, `routes/task-page.js`, `lib/live-console.js`, `lib/timeline-zoom.js`, `lib/run-view.js`, `lib/lineage-membership.js`, `lib/read-horizon.js` and `lib/close-out-events-store.js` is empty. HEAD is `b315e0e8f`, the commit both surveys read.
- I checked live: `GET /cost/LIN-4393` returns the eight lineages in John's drawing. The autopilot has five `wake` dispatches ($0.84 over 63 min). The implementation's `leftover` dispatch at 15:15 costs $1.87 of its $6.95. The other six are single-dispatch sessions. Each dispatch has `requests`, `byModel` and `costUsd`, but no end time. That confirms survey item 1.
- One correction to the surveys: **the task page has no cost read today.** The page and its renderer never mention cost, and the only `readCost` caller with a per-task fetch is the `/cost` route (`routes/proxy-compute.js`), which builds its inputs inline (own rows, the founder lookup, lineage siblings). So "build on the existing cost read" also means "lift that fetch out of the route", or the task page would become a second, hand-copied fetch.
- The page renders for three viewers: `'owner'`, `'member'` and `'guest'` (the `/t/:token` route passes `viewer: 'guest'` and caches and masks page loads). John's ruling: "Owner and members see spend; guests see the picture without dollars".

### The problem, before any solution

A task's sessions run on one clock, but Harbour shows them three ways and none of them shows the whole picture. **Stages** folds orchestration away as check-ins and has no cost. **Live Console** is a 24-hour, now-anchored swimlane with no cost and no working/held split. **`/cost`** has the money and the per-dispatch split but no times past each start. A good outcome is one honest picture per task, built from the facts Harbour already holds, and not a third set of derived meanings. The picture must make waiting look like waiting, so whatever later optimises the graph does not read waiting as cost.

### Shapes considered

**A. Server-rendered lanes from the one cost read (recommended).**
- *How:* lift the `/cost` route's fetch into one lib reader the route and the task page both call. Add each dispatch's first and last request time to `dispatchesOf`. A pure view model turns lineages, dispatches and the merge time into lanes, segments, marks and a scale with breaks. A pure renderer draws them as positioned HTML: percent `left`/`width`, as Live Console's bars are, with no SVG and no client layout math. The page load renders it. A fragment endpoint repaints it on the poll's existing cadence.
- *Cost to build:* moderate. About four small modules and one extraction from the route. *To live with:* low. Every number comes from the read the census already guards, and the view model is golden-testable against LIN-4393.
- *Risks:* one more read per page load. Lineage siblings are capped (`LINEAGE_QUERY_LIMIT`, warn-and-truncate), so a very long-lived lineage can come back incomplete. Its cost then reads "not complete" rather than showing a part sum.
- *Fit:* reuses the one cost read, `cost-format`, the close-out events read the loader already makes, and the page's poll loop. It adds no store and no client framework.

**B. Client-rendered from a JSON endpoint.** The server sends the view model and the browser lays it out, as `public/live-console.js` does.
- With no build step, the scale-with-breaks maths would live in `public/` and be mirrored in `lib/` for tests. That is two copies of one rule, the pattern the `front-end-browser` notes keep logging (`buildDispatchModelOptionDescriptors`, `public/common.js`). It also leaves a guest page empty until the script runs. It buys interactive zoom, which the ask does not need. Rejected.

**C. Extend the Live Console timeline with a task filter** (`buildTimeline`/`packTimelineRows`, `lib/timeline-zoom.js`).
- It works over loops, not lineage records, so it has no per-dispatch cost and no working spans. Its window is 24 hours anchored to now. It drops a wake whose target has aged out. Adding cost to it would make a second cost path, which the census forbids, and merging the two timelines needs its own ruling (global survey, "not this task's"). Rejected.

**D. The underlying refactor: one session-graph model for Stages, Live Console and this picture.** This is the real cause of three drifting answers. Doing it whole means retiring or merging Stages and Live Console, which is "removing a step" and needs a ruling. This task takes the slice that needs no ruling: **one place that says what role a dispatch plays** (below), used by the new view and by Stages' `groupSessions`. Moving Live Console's wake folding onto it is left for later.

### Recommendation: A, with D's slice

**1. One per-task read, whole life.** A new reader (working name `readTaskSessions`, in `lib/task-cost-read.js`) holds the fetch now inline in the `/cost` route: own queued and history rows, founder identity, lineage siblings, then `readCost({ perDispatch: true })`. The route becomes a caller. `lib/read-horizon.js` gains the named rule: *a task's own reads cover its whole life; published reporting windows (periodicals, `/kpis`, workspace spend) stay at 30 days.* The size ruling decided this ("first settling that a task's own views read its whole life rather than the 30-day reporting window"). `/cost/:identifier` is a task's own view, so it adopts the same rule. Its `window` field says so (the planning step picks the exact key; it stays additive). The reads stay bounded by their identity keys: the `{urlKey, issueIdentifier}` history index, uncapped `lineageIdentityRows`, and records loaded by anchor, which were never time-windowed. Stages already reads whole life (`horizon: 'all'`), so the page stops holding two windows. The call-log read (`listInHorizon`) takes the same task-life bound for `/cost`. The timeline itself does not draw Harbour's own calls, since they are not sessions.

**2. Working spans come from the one split.** `dispatchesOf` already gives each request record to exactly one dispatch (split rule C). Each entry gains `firstRequestAt` and `lastRequestAt`, the min and max `at` over the records it owns, or null when it owns none. That is the only new fact, and it is computed where records are already assigned. Nothing else reassigns usage, and the census needs no new exemption. The fields are additive on `/cost` too.

**3. One place for a dispatch's role** (working name `lib/session-roles.js`). `roleOf({ kind, followUpTo })` returns one of four values:
- `wake`: kind `wake`.
- `resumed`: has `followUpTo` and is not a wake. Examples are `leftover`, a ci-wake `custom` row, or a reply follow-up.
- `orchestration`: kind in `ORCHESTRATION_KINDS`, imported from `lib/run-view.js` and not copied.
- `work`: anything else.

A lineage reads as **held** when its base is orchestration and it has wakes. It reads as **fresh** when its base is work. Stages' `groupSessions` switches to the helper. Its current output is pinned by the existing tests and must not change. Per the `runs-and-dispatch` lesson "Row-only kinds stay out of `DISPATCH_KINDS` … kind-keyed maps are tested against both" (LIN-4376), the helper is tested against `DISPATCH_KINDS` and `ROW_ONLY_KINDS`, so `leftover` and `wake` cannot fall through. The waiting entry on `lib/pipeline-churn.js` (its own `ORCHESTRATION_KINDS`, LIN-4376 leftovers) is related. The size of the move does not take it on.

**4. A pure view model** (working name `lib/task-timeline.js`): `taskTimeline({ sessions, mergedAt, now })` returns `{ lanes, scale, marks, totals }`.
- *Lanes:* one per lineage, ordered by start. Each lane carries its kind label, role, model (the cost-dominant one, plus a per-dispatch model when they differ), wall time, worked time (the sum of working spans), cost, and its dispatches.
- *Segments:* a solid **working** segment per dispatch, from first to last request, with a minimum visible width. A thin **held** line runs from the lineage start to its end wherever no dispatch is working. A **running** open end extends to `now`. A dispatch with no records gets no guessed bar. A lineage with no records at all (a snapshot lineage from before records, `dispatches: null`) draws its known start and end as an outline marked "working times unknown", with its snapshot cost.
- *Marks:* a tick per wake (or per resume) at its dispatch time, and a vertical rule at the merge.
- *Scale:* the clock runs from the first dispatch to max(last end, merge, now if live). Any gap where **nothing is working** (no working segment, wake or merge in it) that is longer than a threshold becomes a fixed-width break labelled with its length ("⋯ 2 d 4 h ⋯"). Breaks are computed from working time, not from held spans, so a task that waited two days on a ruling folds that wait into one labelled break. A held line still crosses the break, which is honest about who was holding. The view model sets the threshold (starting at 10 min or 15 % of span), and the LIN-4393 fixture tunes it.
- *Totals:* the sum of fully priced lineages, using the figure rule (never a part sum).

**5. Rendering** (`lib/render-task-timeline.js`, front-end-pages area). It is a new section, **"Sessions on one clock"**, placed under Stages. Stages stays (no removal without a ruling). Each lane is a row:
- *Desktop:* a label column on the left (kind · model · took / worked · cost) and the track on the right, on a shared axis with start and end times and the break labels.
- *Phone* (< 600 px, CSS only): the label goes above a full-width track, so it is the same picture on the same clock with no squeezed text.

Each lane is a `<details>` that opens to its dispatches (kind, started, working span, requests, model, cost), so the detail reads on a phone without hover. Per the `front-end-pages` lesson "A control a page renders per row … needs its own accessible name" (Design & Interface Review, 8 Nov), each lane's `<summary>` carries a full accessible name. Dollars go through `formatUsd` (`lib/cost-format.js`). The page adds `data-testid`s and `data-role`, `data-kind` and `data-state`, and `public/llms.txt` and `docs/architecture/source-map.md` are updated with them.

**6. Spend gating where the data leaves.** The view model is built with costs. One function, `withoutSpend(timeline)`, strips every dollar field. Routes call it for `viewer === 'guest'` before rendering, both on `/t/:token` and on its fragment endpoint, so no dollar figure can reach a guest through markup or `data-*`. Owners and members get the full model. The renderer stays viewer-blind and draws what it is given.

**7. Merge time.** The loader already reads close-out events for `mergedBy` (`readMergedBy`). It returns `prMergedAt` from the same read, so there is no second read. Older events have `prMergedAt: null` (before LIN-3713). For those it falls back to the PR's `merged_at`, which the shared PR status read already returns (`lib/github-pr-status.js`). If neither is known, the picture says "merged, time not recorded" and draws no rule.

**8. Freshness.** The page load renders the section. `public/task-page.js` fetches a new fragment endpoint, `/workspace/:urlKey/api/task/:id/timeline` (and `/t/:token/timeline`), when the poll's track changes or every 60 s while a session runs, so a running bar grows. The `/state` key set, which is pinned, stays untouched. The poll spends no cost read on a quiet task.

**9. Keeping the loader small.** The loader only injects and calls the reader and the view model, and all timeline logic lives in the new modules. New lib files get homes in `docs/areas/areas.json` in the same change: `task-cost-read`, `task-timeline` and `session-roles` go under runs-and-dispatch, and `render-task-timeline` is already front-end-pages by its `render` prefix. This follows the README: "a new production file with no pattern … give it a home in the same change".

**`timeline-zoom.js` is not reused.** Its bounds clamp to `[nowMs − maxSpanMs, nowMs]` with a 24-hour maximum, and its scale is linear. A task's window is fixed, can be days long, and is drawn on a scale with breaks, so neither the bounds nor the maths carry over. The ask does not need zoom. It is left alone, not forked.

**"Every session" for lineages founded elsewhere.** Attribution stays as it is (LIN-4147: a lineage counts under its founder). The per-task read also selects lineages with a member row on this task but a founder elsewhere. An example is a parent's autopilot driving this subtask, or a multi-ticket lane. They are drawn as lanes marked "counted under LIN-X", with their cost shown but left out of this task's total. Only their dispatches tagged with this task set the clock, so a week-long orchestrator does not stretch it. This delivers "every session that ran it" without changing who a lineage's cost counts under. The planning step verifies which rows carry this task's identifier; if wakes carry only the founder's, the lane shows the member dispatches that do.

### Testing

## Part 2 (LIN-4405): how the build departs from the approved plan

PR: https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2390. Each item follows the code, and the reasons are also in the PR.

1. **The fragment cache (resolves the open question from LIN-4405's survey; departs from builder note 5).** Neither fragment uses `cachedLoadPage` (`routes/task-share.js`). That cache holds `loadTaskPage`, which reads the tracker and PR status, and its 5s TTL expires before every poll, so every guest poll would do a full page load and break "fragments make no GitHub calls".
   - Both routes share one single-flight cache instead: `createTimelineFragmentReader` in `lib/task-timeline.js`. It holds the `loadTaskState` open ids plus `readTaskTimeline`, keyed by workspace and task.
   - Its TTL is 30s, below the client's one-fetch-per-60s window. One viewer always gets a fresh read, and any number of tabs (owners, members and guests share the entry) cost at most one read per task per window. The survey suggested a TTL at least as long as the poll interval; I went below it so a single viewer never waits on a stale read.
   - The cache holds the full model. A guest route strips it with `withoutSpend`, which copies.
   - It is registered with the per-key reset (`task-timeline-fragment`, `lib/key-state-holders.js`).
2. **`lineagesTruncated`.** The shared flag alone does not mark this task's total "not complete". Per-lineage `incomplete` is the precise signal: identity rows are uncapped, so a missing member that can change a figure always marks its own lineage, and then `totalUsd` is already null. So a parent's huge lineage pulled in by one wake no longer makes this task's own total read incomplete. The section still shows a note when truncation happened. A lane's start is the earliest of its dispatches, which include members the capped read did not fetch, so its start does not move later without notice.
3. **CI wakes.** A ci-wake `custom` row with `followUpTo` ticks as **resumed** (the approved precedence) and does not make a lineage **held**. Held means an orchestrator that a child held open and woke with `wake` rows. A lineage driven only by CI resumes is labelled by its kind.
4. **Old lineages** (`dispatches: null`) are drawn as an outline over their known span, marked "working times unknown", never as a bar. That is the representation the plan asked for; "without a span" in the earlier comment meant without working spans.
5. **The LIN-4393 fixture corrects one number.** The autopilot's measured work is **2m 22s** (six request spans: the base and five wakes), not the plan's estimate of about 6 min. It was held for 63 min with five wake ticks. The fixture asserts 142s.
6. **Labels** use the app's own stage words (`stageLabel`: Kick-off, Check-in, Build), as Stages does. A lane says "elapsed" (its own start to end) and "worked" (its request spans), never Stages' "took".
7. **The merge fallback** to `pr.mergedAt` is used on page load only, as planned. A fragment repaint reads no GitHub, so where only GitHub knows the merge time, a repaint reads "merged, time not recorded". This is rare: post-LIN-3713 events carry `prMergedAt`, and a merged task usually no longer polls.
8. **Desktop placement.** The page's ≥1024px grid places every child explicitly, so the section gets its own `timeline` grid area directly under `stages` in both templates. Without it, the section rendered above the run control.
